mainTopic: The days of משיח, the hidden reward of עולם הבא, and denying תורה מן השמים
overview: The amud opens with a story: a מין asks רבי אבהו when משיח will come. רבי אבהו answers with a פסוק in ישעיהו about darkness for the nations and light for ישראל. Next comes a long list of opinions on how long ימות המשיח will last. They range from forty years to seven thousand years, and even to as long as all of history. Along the way, רב יוסף rejects רבי הילל's view that there is no future משיח. רבי יוחנן then teaches that the נביאים' promises describe ימות המשיח, בעלי תשובה, and those who support תלמידי חכמים. The greater reward, 'עין לא ראתה', is hidden, and the גמרא discusses what that reward is. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה: one who denies תורה מן השמים has no share in עולם הבא. It brings many readings of 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה', ending with sayings about reviewing one's learning. רבי עקיבא's teaching begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A heretic asks רבי אבהו when משיח will come
steps.stepSummary: A story backs up the earlier teaching: a מין asks when משיח comes, and רבי אבהו answers, 'When darkness covers you people.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what a certain heretic asked רבי אבהו: 'When will משיח come?' He answered: 'When darkness covers those people,' meaning you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that fits the teaching it just gave. A מין asks רבי אבהו when משיח will come, and רבי אבהו gives a pointed answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word והיינו ties this story to the teaching just before it: the day of redemption is light for ישראל but darkness for others. רבי אבהו's answer puts that idea into real life. The coming of משיח goes together with darkness falling on the nations who oppose ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what (this story fits what was just said)

phrases.english: And this is what was said to him
by a certain heretic to Rabbi Abbahu:
When will the Messiah come?
He said to him: When it covers
darkness over those people.
phrases.notes: "Those people" is a polite way of saying "you and your group."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the earlier teaching (just before this text) that redemption brings light to ישראל and darkness to others.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that the day of redemption is darkness for the nations and light for ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exchange between רבי אבהו and a מין.

steps.title: The heretic protests that he is being cursed
steps.stepSummary: The מין complains: 'Are you cursing me?'
steps.simpleTranslation: The heretic said to him: 'Are you cursing me?'
steps.whatsHappening: The מין takes offense at רבי אבהו's answer and accuses him of cursing him. This sets up רבי אבהו's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The protest is that the answer sounds like a personal insult with no basis. רבי אבהו now has to show that he is not making this up. He is only repeating what a פסוק says.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵילָט קָא לָיְיטַתְּ לִי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Are you cursing me?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵילָט קָא לָיְיטַתְּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רבי אבהו's answer in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's answer that משיח comes when darkness covers the מין's people.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer seems to be a personal curse with no source behind it.

steps.title: רבי אבהו shows his answer comes from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that he is only quoting ישעיהו: darkness covers the earth, but ה׳ shines on ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a written פסוק: 'For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and thick fog the nations; but ה׳ will shine upon you, and His glory will be seen upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו defends himself. He says he is not cursing anyone; he is quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes two things at the same time: darkness for the nations and light for ישראל. So 'darkness on those people' is simply the other side of ישראל's redemption, as the נביא described it. It is not a private curse.
steps.whatToRemember: The coming of משיח is pictured as darkness for the nations and light for ישראל, based on ישעיהו.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a written verse,
"For behold, the darkness shall cover the earth,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 60:2

phrases.english: and thick fog the nations;
but upon you the Lord will shine,
and His glory will be seen upon you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מין's complaint from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source citation: the statement is a quote from a פסוק, not a personal curse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבהו was cursing the מין on his own.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was repeating ישעיהו's prophecy that darkness covers the nations while ה׳ shines on ישראל.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the days of משיח last forty years
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר's view that the days of משיח last forty years, based on תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says the days of משיח are forty years, as the פסוק says: 'Forty years I will strive with the generation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא: how long will the days of משיח last? The first opinion is רבי אליעזר's: forty years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learns the number from a פסוק that mentions forty years with a generation. Just as the desert period lasted forty years, the days of משיח will also be a set period of forty years. This opens a list of opinions about the length.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says,
the days of the Messiah are forty years,
as it is said: "Forty years I will strive with the generation."
phrases.notes: תהלים 95:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: the length of the days of משיח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days of משיח last forty years.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: seventy years
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says seventy years, reading 'one king' in ישעיהו as the special king, משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: seventy years, as it says: 'And on that day צור will be forgotten seventy years, like the days of one king.' Which king is special and unique? You must say: this is משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא: the days of משיח last seventy years. He also explains why the פסוק is talking about משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of seventy years 'like the days of one king.' He reads 'one' (אחד) as 'unique' (מיוחד). The one truly unique king is משיח, so the seventy years are the days of משיח.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר, שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: seventy years,
as it is said: "And it shall be on that day
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 23:15

phrases.english: that Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years,
like the days of one king."
Which is the unique king?
phrases.notes: The word "one" in the פסוק is being read as "unique, one of a kind."

phrases.english: You must say: this is the Messiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר, שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different length than רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days of משיח last seventy years.

steps.title: רבי: three generations
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the days of משיח last three generations, learned from 'דור דורים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: three generations, as it says: 'They will fear You as long as the sun, and before the moon, a generation of generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the ברייתא: רבי says the days of משיח last three generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count comes from the words דור דורים. דור is one generation, and דורים (plural) is at least two more. Together that makes three generations.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: three generations,
phrases.notes: "רבי" by itself means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: as it is said: "They shall fear You with the sun,
phrases.notes: תהלים 72:5

phrases.english: and before the moon, a generation of generations."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view on the length of the days of משיח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days of משיח last three generations.

steps.title: רבי הילל: there is no future משיח
steps.stepSummary: רבי הילל says ישראל will have no future משיח, because they already 'ate' him in the days of חזקיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הילל says: There is no משיח for ישראל, because they already consumed him in the days of חזקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: A very different opinion: רבי הילל says no משיח will come in the future at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They already ate him' means the good promised for the days of משיח was already used up in the days of חזקיה. So according to him, nothing is left for a future משיח. This sets up רב יוסף's strong reply.

keyTerms.meaning: They ate him (they already used up his blessings)

steps.confusionAlert: This רבי הילל is a later sage, not the famous הלל הזקן. Also, the גמרא does not leave his view standing; רב יוסף rejects it right away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hillel says:
There is no Messiah for Israel,
for they already ate him in the days of Hezekiah.
phrases.notes: "Ate him" means they already enjoyed all the good that was promised with משיח.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי הִילֵּל אוֹמֵר: אֵין לָהֶם מָשִׁיחַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how long משיח's days last to whether a future משיח comes at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no future משיח; the promises were fulfilled in the days of חזקיה.

steps.title: רב יוסף rejects רבי הילל using זכריה's prophecy
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says 'May his Master forgive רבי הילל': חזקיה lived in the first בית המקדש period, but זכריה, in the second, still promised a coming king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: May his Master forgive רבי הילל. When did חזקיה live? In the time of the first בית המקדש! But זכריה prophesied in the time of the second בית המקדש and said: 'Rejoice greatly, daughter of ציון; shout, daughter of ירושלים; behold, your king will come to you, righteous and victorious, poor and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף strongly rejects רבי הילל's view. He proves from history and a פסוק that a king, משיח, was still expected after חזקיה's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the promises of משיח had been used up in חזקיה's days, a later נביא would not predict a coming king. But זכריה lived long after חזקיה, during the second בית המקדש, and still announced 'your king will come to you.' So the days of משיח are still in the future.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף proves from זכריה, who prophesied after חזקיה, that משיח is still to come. רבי הילל's view is rejected.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rejection keeps in place the basic belief that משיח will come in the future.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
May his Master forgive Rabbi Hillel.
phrases.notes: "His Master" means ה׳. It is a gentle way of saying רבי הילל spoke wrongly here.

phrases.english: Hezekiah, when was he? In the First Temple period!

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ זְכַרְיָה קָא מִתְנַבֵּי בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי, וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Whereas Zechariah prophesied in the Second Temple period, and said:
"Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion;
phrases.notes: זכריה 9:9

phrases.english: shout, daughter of Jerusalem;
behold, your king will come to you;
he is righteous and victorious,
poor and riding upon a donkey,
and upon a colt, the foal of a donkey."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: שְׁרָא לֵיהּ מָרֵיהּ לְרַבִּי הִילֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי הילל's view from step 7.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A נביא who lived after חזקיה still promised a coming king, so the promises of משיח could not have been used up in חזקיה's time.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי הילל's claim that משיח was already 'eaten' in the days of חזקיה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Timeline: זכריה, in the second בית המקדש period, prophesied about a future king long after חזקיה.

steps.title: Another source for forty years: the desert and the days of suffering
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר's forty-year view, now proven by matching the word for 'afflict' in דברים and in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says the days of משיח are forty years. Here it says 'He afflicted you, let you hunger and fed you' (about the forty years in the desert). There it says 'Make us glad according to the days You afflicted us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא that gives רבי אליעזר's same forty-year opinion, but with a new proof. The proof links the forty years of suffering in the desert to the days of joy we ask for in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same root, 'afflict' (ענה), appears in both פסוקים. In דברים it describes the forty years in the desert. In תהלים we ask ה׳ to give us joy for as long as we were afflicted, so the good days of משיח equal those forty years.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here (the first פסוק of a comparison)
And it is written there (the matching פסוק)
Affliction, suffering; the shared word that links the פסוקים

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of step 4. It gives the same number, forty years, but here the proof comes from matching a word in דברים with the פסוק in תהלים.

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
Rabbi Eliezer says,
The days of Mashiach are forty years.
It is written here:
"And He afflicted you, and let you hunger, and fed you",
phrases.notes: דברים 8:3. This is about the forty years in the desert, when they ate the מן.

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"Make us glad according to the days You afflicted us,
the years we saw evil."
phrases.notes: תהלים 90:15

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי אליעזר's forty-year view from step 4 and gives a second ברייתא with a different proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days of משיח last forty years, matching the forty years of suffering in the desert.

steps.title: Four hundred years: matching the suffering in מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא says four hundred years, linking the four hundred years of slavery promised to אברהם with the פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: four hundred years. Here it says 'They will enslave them and afflict them four hundred years.' There it says 'Make us glad according to the days You afflicted us.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא uses the same method as רבי אליעזר but picks a different time of suffering. He picks the four hundred years of slavery foretold to אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions use the word 'afflict' to link to 'Make us glad according to the days You afflicted us.' They disagree only about which suffering the פסוק in תהלים means: the desert (forty years) or the slavery (four hundred years).

keyTerms.meaning: And they will enslave them and afflict them (said at the ברית בין הבתרים)

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
Four hundred years.
It is written here:
"And they will enslave them and afflict them
four hundred years",
phrases.notes: בראשית 15:13

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"Make us glad according to the days You afflicted us."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same word-match as step 9 but links it to the slavery in מצרים instead of the desert.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days of משיח last four hundred years, matching the years of slavery.

steps.title: 365 years, like the days of the solar year
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the days of משיח last 365 years, the number of days in a solar year, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: 365 years, like the number of days in the sun's year, as it says: 'For a day of vengeance is in My heart, and the year of My redeemed has come.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a third number, 365 years. He brings a פסוק in ישעיהו that speaks of a 'day' and a 'year' of redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי does not use the 'afflict' comparison at all. He reads the 'year' of redemption in ישעיהו as hinting at the 365 days of a solar year, with each day standing for one year of redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of the solar year (365)
A day of vengeance against the enemies of ישראל
The year of My redeemed ones

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: Just 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who wrote down the משנה.

phrases.english: Three hundred sixty-five years,
like the number of days of the solar year,
as it is said:
"For a day of vengeance is in My heart,
and the year of My redeemed has come."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 63:4

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשִׁשִּׁים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion in the same ברייתא, using a different kind of proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days of משיח last 365 years, like the days of a solar year.

steps.title: What does 'a day of vengeance is in My heart' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what it means that the day of vengeance is 'in My heart.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'a day of vengeance is in My heart' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the words of רבי's פסוק. This question sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'in My heart' is unusual when said about ה׳. The גמרא wants to know what it teaches about the day of redemption.

phrases.english: What is "a day of vengeance is in My heart"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the פסוק רבי quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'in My heart' mean about the day of vengeance.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: told to My heart, not to My limbs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that ה׳ kept the day of redemption in His 'heart' and did not reveal it to His 'limbs.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: I revealed it to My heart; I did not reveal it to My limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. 'In My heart' means the date of redemption is a hidden secret.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speaking as if ה׳ had a body, רבי יוחנן says the date was kept inside, in the 'heart,' and never passed on to the 'limbs.' In other words, ה׳ never said the date out loud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
To My heart I revealed it,
to My limbs I did not reveal it.
phrases.notes: This is said as if ה׳ had a body. He means the secret never left the 'heart,' so ה׳ never said it out loud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The date of redemption is kept in ה׳'s 'heart' and was never revealed to His 'limbs,' so it was never said out loud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: told to My heart, not to the angels
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the secret was not revealed even to the ministering angels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: I revealed it to My heart; I did not reveal it to the ministering angels.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a second explanation of 'in My heart.' He says not even the angels know the date of redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree the date is a secret. ריש לקיש makes the point even stronger: the date is hidden even from the angels, who serve before ה׳.
steps.whatToRemember: There are many opinions about how long the days of משיח last, including forty years, seventy years, three generations, four hundred years, and 365 years. And 'a day of vengeance is in My heart' teaches that the time of redemption is a secret kept by ה׳ alone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
To My heart I revealed it,
to the ministering angels I did not reveal it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לְלִבִּי גִּלִּיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 12, alongside רבי יוחנן's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The date of redemption was not revealed even to the ministering angels.

steps.title: אבימי: ימות המשיח last seven thousand years
steps.stepSummary: אבימי בריה דרבי אבהו teaches that ימות המשיח will last seven thousand years. He bases this on the פסוק comparing ה׳'s joy over ישראל to a groom's joy over his bride.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי, son of רבי אבהו, taught: ימות המשיח for ישראל will be seven thousand years, as it says: 'As a groom rejoices over his bride, so will your God rejoice over you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another opinion to the list of how long ימות המשיח will last. This one is seven thousand years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חתן's celebration with his כלה lasts seven days, and one "day" of ה׳ is a thousand years. So the פסוק hints at seven of ה׳'s days, which is seven thousand years. This is much longer than the earlier numbers of four hundred years and 365 years.

keyTerms.meaning: the days of משיח, the era after the redemption
as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: Avimi, son of Rabbi Abbahu, taught:
The days of Moshiach for Israel
are seven thousand years,
as it is said: "And as a groom rejoices over a bride,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 62:5. A groom celebrates for seven days, and a "day" for ה׳ is a thousand years.

phrases.english: so will your God rejoice over you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list of opinions on the length of ימות המשיח (steps 10-11), after the side discussion in steps 12-14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ימות המשיח last seven thousand years, learned from the seven days of a groom's celebration.

steps.title: שמואל: as long as from creation until now
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: ימות המשיח will last as long as all the time from the creation of the world until now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: ימות המשיח will be as long as the time from the day the world was created until now, as it says: 'like the days of the heavens over the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion on the length of ימות המשיח. This one says it will equal all of history so far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises the people will last in the land 'like the days of the heavens over the earth.' The heavens have stood over the earth since creation, so ימות המשיח will match that span, from creation until משיח comes.

keyTerms.meaning: like (the time) from the day the world was created
like the days of the heavens

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The days of Moshiach
are like from the day the world was created until now,
as it is said: "like the days of the heavens over the earth."
phrases.notes: דברים 11:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another opinion to the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ימות המשיח equal the span from creation until משיח comes.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: as long as from נח until now
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says ימות המשיח will last as long as the time from נח until now. He reads 'כי מי נח' as 'כימי נח', meaning 'like the days of נח.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: like the days from נח until now, as it says: 'For this is like the waters of נח to Me, as I have sworn.'
steps.whatsHappening: One more opinion on the length of ימות המשיח. This one counts from the time of נח instead of from creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיהו is about the redemption. The words 'כי מי נח' (for the waters of נח) can be read as one word, 'כימי נח', meaning 'like the days of נח.' So the redemption will last as long as the time from נח until משיח.

keyTerms.meaning: נח, from the time of the flood
'for the waters of' read as 'like the days of'

steps.whatToRemember: The opinions on the length of ימות המשיח so far: forty years, seventy years, three generations, 400 years, 365 years, 7,000 years, from creation until now, and from נח until now. Each one comes from a different פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Like the days from Noach until now,
as it is said: "For this is like the waters of Noach to Me,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 54:9. He reads 'כי מי' (for the waters of) as one word, 'כימי' (like the days of).

phrases.english: as I have sworn."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different starting point from שמואל's: נח instead of creation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ימות המשיח equal the span from נח until משיח comes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the נביאים only spoke about ימות המשיח
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: all the נביאים prophesied only about ימות המשיח. The reward of עולם הבא is something no eye has seen except ה׳'s.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: all the נביאים prophesied only about ימות המשיח. But about עולם הבא it says: 'No eye has seen it, God, except You, what He will do for those who wait for Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks what the good things promised by the נביאים are about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says every good promise in the נביאים describes ימות המשיח. עולם הבא is so great that no נביא could see it, and only ה׳ knows it. This means the wonderful descriptions in the נביאים belong to ימות המשיח.

keyTerms.meaning: for the one who waits for Him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ימות המשיח and עולם הבא. Here they are two different stages. רבי יוחנן puts the נביאים' promises in the first and says the second is beyond what any נביא saw.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
All the prophets, every one of them,
prophesied only about the days of Moshiach,
but about the World to Come:
"No eye has seen it, God, except You,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 64:3

phrases.english: what God will do for the one who waits for Him."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the length of ימות המשיח to what the נביאים' prophecies describe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the נביאים' prophecies are about ימות המשיח. עולם הבא is beyond any prophecy.

steps.title: This argues with שמואל, who says only foreign rule will end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן argues with שמואל. שמואל holds that the only difference between this world and ימות המשיח is that ישראל will no longer be ruled by other kingdoms.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this argues with שמואל, for שמואל said: there is no difference between this world and ימות המשיח except the rule of other kingdoms over ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן's teaching does not fit with what שמואל holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, ימות המשיח hold all the wonders the נביאים describe. For שמואל, ימות המשיח look like this world, except that ישראל is free. So שמואל would have to say that the wonderful promises in the נביאים are about עולם הבא.
steps.whatToRemember: Two views of ימות המשיח: רבי יוחנן sees it as the time of all the נביאים' wonders. שמואל sees it as normal life, just without foreign rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic argument about what ימות המשיח will look like. Later discussions about the redemption come back to it often.

phrases.english: And this argues with Shmuel,
for Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ
phrases.english: There is no difference between this world and the days of Moshiach
except being ruled by other kingdoms alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that שמואל disagrees with רבי יוחנן's teaching in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: the only difference between this world and ימות המשיח is the end of foreign rule over ישראל. This argues with רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The prophets spoke about penitents; the reward of the fully righteous is beyond description
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: the נביאים' promises were only about בעלי תשובה. The reward of צדיקים גמורים is so great that no eye has seen it except ה׳'s.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: All the נביאים prophesied only about people who did תשובה. But for the completely righteous, the reward is 'No eye has seen it, God, except You.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new teaching, built just like his teaching in Step 18. This time he compares בעלי תשובה with צדיקים גמורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The good things the נביאים described are the reward of בעלי תשובה. The reward of צדיקים גמורים is too great for any נביא to describe, so only ה׳ knows it. This means רבי יוחנן ranks צדיקים גמורים above בעלי תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: People who sinned and then did teshuvah (penitents)
Completely righteous people who never sinned
'No eye has seen': a reward hidden from everyone except ה׳

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
All the prophets did not prophesy
except about people who did teshuvah,
but about completely righteous people,
"No eye has seen it, God, except You."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 64:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from רבי יוחנן built like Step 18, now comparing בעלי תשובה with צדיקים גמורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נביאים' promises were about בעלי תשובה. The reward of צדיקים גמורים is hidden and beyond description.

steps.title: רב: penitents stand where the righteous cannot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן argues with רבי אבהו. רבי אבהו quotes רב: the righteous cannot stand in the place where בעלי תשובה stand. רב brings a פסוק from ישעיהו as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this argues with רבי אבהו. רבי אבהו said in the name of רב: In the place where people who did תשובה stand, the צדיקים cannot stand, as it says: 'Peace, peace to the far and to the near.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן's teaching argues with another opinion. It then quotes רב, who holds the opposite: בעלי תשובה are on a higher level than צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, צדיקים גמורים are higher. For רב, בעלי תשובה reach a place that even צדיקים cannot reach. רב's source is the פסוק 'שלום שלום לרחוק ולקרוב', and the next step explains how it proves his point.

keyTerms.meaning: And it argues: this statement disagrees with another one
Standing: here it means a spiritual level or rank
'To the far and to the near'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. רבי יוחנן ranks the צדיק higher, and רב (quoted by רבי אבהו) ranks the בעל תשובה higher.

phrases.english: And this argues with Rabbi Abahu,
for Rabbi Abahu said that Rav said:
In the place where people who did teshuvah stand,
the righteous cannot stand there,
as it says:
"Peace, peace to the far and to the near."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 57:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows an opinion that argues with רבי יוחנן's ranking from Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בעלי תשובה stand on a level that צדיקים cannot reach.

steps.title: How the verse shows the penitent comes first
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק greets the 'far' person first and the 'near' person second. 'Far' means someone who was once far from ה׳, a בעל תשובה. 'Near' means someone who was always near, a צדיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: First it says 'far,' and then 'near.' What is 'far'? Someone who was far at first. And what is 'near'? Someone who was near at first and is still near now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב's פסוק proves his point. The order of the words shows who gets greeted first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever is greeted first is the more important one. Since 'far' comes first and means the בעל תשובה, the בעל תשובה is placed above the צדיק, who is the 'near' one.

phrases.english: First it says "far,"
and only then "near."
What is "far"?
Someone who was far at first.
And what is "near"?
Someone who was near at first and is still near now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in Step 21 proves רב's view.
steps.raayaObject: That בעלי תשובה are on a higher level than צדיקים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word order of ישעיהו 57:19: 'far' (the בעל תשובה) is greeted before 'near' (the צדיק).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reads 'far' and 'near' the other way
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the פסוק differently. 'Far' means far from sin, which is the צדיק. 'Near' means someone who was close to sin and pulled away, which is the בעל תשובה. So the צדיק is greeted first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: 'To the far' means someone who is far from sin. 'Near' means someone who was near to sin and then distanced himself from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן shows that the same פסוק fits his own view. He flips the meanings of 'far' and 'near.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב read 'far' as far from ה׳‎. רבי יוחנן reads it as far from sin, which describes the צדיק. Now the צדיק is greeted first, and רב's proof no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: And he distanced himself from it

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides read the same פסוק. רב says 'far' is the בעל תשובה and is greeted first, so he is greater. רבי יוחנן says 'far' is the צדיק, far from sin, so the צדיק is greater.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:
"To the far" means one who is far from sin,
"Near" means one who was near to sin
and distanced himself from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לָרָחוֹק שֶׁהוּא רָחוֹק מֵעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's proof in Step 22 by reading the פסוק the other way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב's reading of the פסוק, not the פסוק itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Far' can mean far from sin (the צדיק), so the word order actually puts the צדיק first.

steps.title: Supporters of Torah scholars and the scholars themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the נביאים' promises were about people who support a תלמיד חכם. Such a person might marry his daughter to one, do business on his behalf, or let him benefit from his property. The reward of the תלמידי חכמים themselves is 'עין לא ראתה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: All the נביאים prophesied only about someone who marries his daughter to a תלמיד חכם, someone who does business for a תלמיד חכם, and someone who lets a תלמיד חכם benefit from his property. But for תלמידי חכמים themselves: 'No eye has seen it, God, except You.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third teaching from רבי יוחנן built the same way. Now he compares those who support a תלמיד חכם with the תלמיד חכם himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Supporting Torah scholars earns the great rewards the נביאים described. The reward of the תלמידי חכמים themselves is even greater and hidden from everyone but ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: One who marries off his daughter
And one who gives benefit to

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is a well-known source for the great value of supporting Torah learners.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
All the prophets, every one of them, did not prophesy
except about one who marries his daughter to a Torah scholar,
and about one who does business for a Torah scholar,
and about one who lets a Torah scholar benefit from his property.
But Torah scholars themselves:
"No eye has seen it, God, except You."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כׇּל הַנְּבִיאִים כּוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from רבי יוחנן built the same way as Steps 18 and 20, now about supporting תלמידי חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Supporters of תלמידי חכמים receive the rewards the נביאים described. The reward of the תלמידי חכמים themselves is hidden and beyond description.

steps.title: What is the hidden reward 'no eye has seen'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reward the phrase 'עין לא ראתה' is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'No eye has seen'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the phrase repeated in the last few teachings. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know what this hidden reward actually is. Two אמוראים answer in the next steps.

phrases.english: What is "No eye has seen"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the phrase used in Steps 18, 20 and 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reward is meant by 'עין לא ראתה'

steps.title: Wine kept in its grapes since creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that 'עין לא ראתה' is wine that has been kept inside its grapes since the six days of creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: This is wine kept in its grapes since the six days of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives the first answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This wine has never been squeezed out or tasted by any person. So no one knows how good it is, which fits 'no eye has seen.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
This is wine kept in its grapes
since the six days of creation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hidden reward is wine kept in its grapes since creation.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: it is עדן, which no eye ever saw
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers differently: 'עין לא ראתה' is עדן, a place no eye has ever seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This is עדן, which no eye has ever seen.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the hidden reward is a place, עדן, that no person has ever seen. This raises a question about אדם הראשון, which the next steps deal with.

keyTerms.meaning: Eden: a special place, different from the garden

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
This is Eden,
which no eye has ever seen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 25 that differs from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hidden reward is עדן, which no eye has ever seen.

steps.title: אדם lived in the גן, not in עדן itself
steps.stepSummary: Someone might ask: didn't אדם הראשון live in עדן, so he saw it? The answer: אדם lived in the גן, not in עדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: Where did אדם live? In the גן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a question someone might ask about ריש לקיש's answer and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אדם lived in עדן, then some eye did see it. The answer is that אדם lived in the גן, so no person ever saw עדן itself.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a question someone might raise

phrases.english: And if you will say:
Where did Adam live?
phrases.notes: The question is: if אדם lived in עדן, then someone did see it.

phrases.english: In the garden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends ריש לקיש's answer in Step 27 against a question someone might raise.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction: the גן and עדן are different places
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אדם lived in עדן, so a human eye did see it.
steps.terutzMaskana: אדם lived in the גן, so no eye ever saw עדן.

steps.title: A פסוק shows the גן and עדן are two places
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say the גן and עדן are the same place. The פסוק 'a river goes out from עדן to water the גן' shows they are two separate places.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: The גן is עדן? The פסוק teaches: 'And a river goes out from עדן to water the גן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers one more question someone might ask: maybe the גן is the same as עדן. It brings a פסוק to prove they are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A river goes out from one place to water another place, so the פסוק must be describing two places. This backs up the answer in Step 28 that אדם never saw עדן.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a proof from a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views of 'עין לא ראתה': רבי יהושע בן לוי says it is wine kept since creation, and ריש לקיש says it is עדן. עדן is separate from the גן where אדם lived, so no one has ever seen it.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
The garden is Eden?
The verse teaches:
"And a river goes out from Eden to water the garden."
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the distinction used in Step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That the גן and עדן are two separate places
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 2:10: a river goes out from עדן to water the גן

steps.title: The משנה's next case: denying that the Torah is from heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case from the משנה: one who says the תורה is not from heaven has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one who says the תורה is not from heaven,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of עדן and goes back to the משנה to start a new section. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a quote from the משנה, not a new teaching. It names the next person who loses עולם הבא: someone who denies that the תורה came from הקדוש ברוך הוא. The next steps will look for the source in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The belief that the תורה comes from heaven, given by הקדוש ברוך הוא
'And so on.' The rest of the quote is left out.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאוֹמֵר: אֵין תּוֹרָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: And one who says: the Torah is not from heaven, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה's list of people who have no share in the World-to-Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of עדן and goes back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who denies תורה מן השמים has no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: The verse behind the ruling: 'he despised the word of God'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה... הכרת תכרת' as talking about one who denies תורה מן השמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Because he despised the word of ה׳ and broke His command, he shall surely be cut off.' This is someone who says the תורה is not from heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the פסוק that the משנה's ruling comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a person who despises 'the word of ה׳.' The ברייתא says the clearest example is someone who denies that the תורה is God's word at all. The punishment in the פסוק, being 'cut off,' fits losing עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall surely be cut off.' This is the punishment of כרת.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "Because he despised the word of the Lord
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:31

phrases.english: and broke His commandment, he shall surely be cut off"

phrases.aramaic: – זֶה הָאוֹמֵר: אֵין תּוֹרָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם.
phrases.english: – this is one who says: the Torah is not from heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the line of the משנה just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that one who denies תורה מן השמים loses עולם הבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 15:31, 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה... הכרת תכרת'

steps.title: Another reading: the פסוק is about an אפיקורוס
steps.stepSummary: A second reading says 'despised the word of ה׳' refers to an אפיקורוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Because he despised the word of ה׳' is an אפיקורוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a different person who fits the same פסוק: an אפיקורוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'despised the word of ה׳' can describe more than one kind of person. Here they describe someone who treats God's word and its teachers with contempt, not only someone who denies where the תורה came from.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Another explanation.' This brings a different reading of the same פסוק.
One who treats the תורה and its scholars with contempt

phrases.english: Another explanation: "Because he despised the word of the Lord"
– this is an apikoros.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״כִּי דְבַר ה׳ בָּזָה״ – זֶה אֶפִּיקוֹרוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה' refers to an אפיקורוס.

steps.title: A third reading: twisting the Torah, undoing circumcision, and the double 'cut off'
steps.stepSummary: A third reading splits the פסוק: 'despised the word' is one who twists the meaning of the תורה, 'broke His command' is one who undoes ברית מילה, and the doubled 'cut off' means this world and עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'despised the word of ה׳' is one who twists the meaning of the תורה. 'Broke His command' is one who breaks the covenant of the flesh. 'He shall surely be cut off': cut off in this world, and cut off from עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads each part of the פסוק as a separate case and explains why the word for 'cut off' appears twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'despised the word' is about someone who misreads the תורה on purpose, and 'broke His command' is about ברית מילה. The doubled verb הכרת תכרת is read as two punishments: one in this world and one in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: One who twists the meaning of the תורה in ways that go against the הלכה
One who breaks the covenant of the flesh, meaning ברית מילה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves of הכרת תכרת. The first word means being cut off in this world. The second means being cut off from עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "Because he despised the word of the Lord"
– this is one who reveals aspects in the Torah.
phrases.notes: He means someone who twists the תורה's meaning in a way that goes against the הלכה, as the next step spells out.

phrases.english: "And broke His commandment"
– this is one who breaks the covenant of the flesh.
"He shall surely be cut off" –
"cut off" in this world,
"shall be cut off" from the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״כִּי דְבַר ה׳ בָּזָה״ – זֶה הַמְגַלֶּה פָּנִים בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same פסוק, now explaining each part separately.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twisting the תורה and undoing ברית מילה bring a double כרת: in this world and from עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר המודעי's list of five who lose עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: Based on this פסוק, רבי אלעזר המודעי lists five sinners who lose עולם הבא even if they have תורה and good deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here רבי אלעזר המודעי said: one who treats holy things as ordinary, one who treats the מועדים with contempt, one who breaks the covenant of אברהם אבינו, one who twists the תורה against the הלכה, and one who embarrasses his friend in public. Even if he has תורה and good deeds, he has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר המודעי builds a full list from the פסוק, adding cases that are not directly in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'from here' shows the list grows out of the reading in the last step. The striking point is the ending: even a person full of תורה and good deeds loses עולם הבא for these sins. Embarrassing someone in public is placed on the same level as the others.

keyTerms.meaning: One who treats holy items, such as קרבנות, as ordinary
One who treats the festival days with contempt
One who embarrasses his friend, literally 'makes his face turn white'

steps.whatToRemember: These five sins cost a person עולם הבא even if he has תורה and good deeds, including embarrassing someone in public.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the well-known source showing how serious it is to embarrass another person in public.

phrases.english: From here Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i said:
One who desecrates the consecrated items,
and one who treats the festivals with contempt,
and one who breaks the covenant of Abraham our forefather,
and one who reveals aspects in the Torah not in accordance with halakha,
and one who humiliates his fellow in public,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ תּוֹרָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים
phrases.english: even though he has Torah and good deeds to his credit,
he has no share in the World-to-Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a wider list of sinners from the reading in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These five sinners lose עולם הבא despite having תורה and good deeds.

steps.title: Denying even one verse counts as denying the Torah
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that even someone who accepts the whole תורה except one פסוק, claiming משה made it up himself, falls under 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: 'Because he despised the word of ה׳' is one who says the תורה is not from heaven. Even if he says the whole תורה is from heaven except this one פסוק, which הקדוש ברוך הוא did not say and משה said on his own, this is 'Because he despised the word of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא repeats the basic reading and then stretches it: denying even a single פסוק is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You do not have to reject the whole תורה to be included. Saying that even one פסוק came from משה and not from הקדוש ברוך הוא means you have denied תורה מן השמים.

keyTerms.meaning: On his own, from his own mouth

phrases.english: Another baraita taught: "Because he despised the word of the Lord"

phrases.aramaic: – זֶה הָאוֹמֵר אֵין תּוֹרָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם.
phrases.english: – this is one who says the Torah is not from heaven.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ אָמַר כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: And even if he said the entire Torah is from heaven,
except for this verse
which the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not say
but Moses said it on his own
– this is "Because he despised the word of the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that agrees with step 31 and widens it to cover even a single פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Denying the divine source of even one פסוק counts as denying תורה מן השמים.

steps.title: Even denying one rule learned from the text counts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes further: denying even one דקדוק, קל וחומר or גזירה שוה is also 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if he says the whole תורה is from heaven except this small detail learned from the wording, this קל וחומר, or this גזירה שוה, this is 'Because he despised the word of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא takes one more step: even the rules the חכמים learn from the words of the פסוקים are part of the תורה from heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now it is not even a whole פסוק being denied, only a teaching drawn out of one. The ברייתא treats these methods of learning as part of God's word, so rejecting one of them is like rejecting the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine point learned from the exact wording of a פסוק
A 'how much more so' argument, from a lighter case to a stricter one
A teaching learned by connecting matching words in two פסוקים

steps.whatToRemember: Denying the תורה includes denying one פסוק, or even one rule the חכמים learn from it.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ אָמַר כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: And even if he said the entire Torah is from heaven,
except for this fine inference,
except for this a fortiori argument,
except for this verbal analogy
– this is "Because he despised the word of the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ אָמַר כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, חוּץ מִדִּקְדּוּק זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens step 35 from a whole פסוק to a single teaching drawn from the text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rejecting even one דקדוק, קל וחומר or גזירה שוה counts as 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה.'

steps.title: רבי מאיר: one who learns but does not teach
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that one who learns תורה but does not teach it to others is 'despising the word of ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר used to say, one who learns תורה and does not teach it, this is 'He despised the word of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא applies the פסוק to a person who keeps his תורה to himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves away from belief and toward behavior. Keeping תורה to yourself and not passing it on shows you do not value it enough, which רבי מאיר counts as despising God's word.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
One who learns Torah and does not teach it
– this is "he despised the word of the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that reads the same פסוק as being about neglecting to teach תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה without teaching it is 'דבר ה׳ בזה.'

steps.title: רבי נתן: one who does not pay attention to the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says the פסוק refers to anyone who does not pay attention to the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: anyone who does not pay attention to the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן gives his own example of who is 'despising the word of ה׳.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן, ignoring the משנה, the main body of the הלכה, is treating God's word lightly.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל הַמִּשְׁנָה.
phrases.english: Anyone who does not pay attention to the Mishnah.
phrases.notes: The words 'this is "he despised the word of the Lord"' are left out, but they are understood from רבי מאיר's line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different opinion in the same ברייתא as רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not paying attention to the משנה is 'דבר ה׳ בזה.'

steps.title: רבי נהוראי: one who could learn תורה but does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי נהוראי says the פסוק refers to anyone who is able to learn תורה and does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נהוראי says: anyone who is able to learn תורה and does not learn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נהוראי gives the widest reading: just having the chance to learn and not using it is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three opinions get wider as they go: not teaching, then ignoring the משנה, then not learning at all when you could. רבי נהוראי's view covers any able person who neglects learning.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible, he is able
To be busy with learning תורה

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה' covers denying the תורה, and it is also stretched to people who neglect teaching, the משנה, or learning when they are able.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nehorai says:
Anyone for whom it is possible to engage in Torah
and he does not engage in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the same ברייתא, the widest of the three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who is able to learn תורה and does not is 'דבר ה׳ בזה.'

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the verse refers to an idol worshipper
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says that 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה' refers to someone who worships עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: This verse is talking about someone who worships idols.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more opinion on who is meant by 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה.' רבי ישמעאל says it is someone who serves עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier opinions applied the פסוק to people who deny parts of the תורה or neglect learning. רבי ישמעאל reads it very differently, as referring to the most basic sin against ה׳, which is idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who serves or worships

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
This is one who worships idols.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the פסוק we have been discussing: 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: זֶה הָעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another opinion to the list of interpretations of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה' refers to an idol worshipper.

steps.title: Where in the verse is this seen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק shows that it is talking about idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: What in the verse implies this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי ישמעאל's reading. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'despising the word of ה׳' do not obviously mention idols. So the גמרא wants to know which part of the wording points to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its implication? Where is this seen in the text?

phrases.english: What is its implication?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of רבי ישמעאל's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words in 'כי דבר ה׳ בזה' point to idol worship.

steps.title: The 'word of God' is the first statement at סיני
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי ישמעאל's school explains that the 'word of ה׳' means the statement at סיני, 'אנכי ה׳ אלקיך, לא יהיה לך אלהים אחרים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'Because he despised the word of God' means someone who despises the statement said to משה at סיני: 'I am the Lord your God,' and 'You shall have no other gods.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. 'The word of ה׳' is a specific statement, the one at סיני that forbids other gods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דבר ה׳' is read as a particular 'דבור,' the famous statement 'אנכי ה׳ אלקיך, לא יהיה לך.' Someone who serves idols is treating that exact statement with contempt. That is how the פסוק points to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל (a ברייתא)
'I am', the opening word of the עשרת הדברות

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל reads 'דבר ה׳' as the statement at סיני, 'אנכי ה׳ אלקיך, לא יהיה לך.' So despising it means worshipping עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'Because he despised the word of the Lord'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:31

phrases.english: this is one who despises the statement
that was said to Moshe from Sinai:
'I am the Lord your God,'
phrases.notes: שמות 20:2–3

phrases.english: 'You shall have no other gods,' etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41 by citing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'דבר ה׳' means the specific statement at סיני forbidding other gods, so despising it means idol worship.

steps.title: Learning without reviewing is like sowing without reaping
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה compares someone who learns תורה but does not review it to a farmer who plants but never harvests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: Anyone who learns תורה and does not review it is like a person who plants and does not harvest.
steps.whatsHappening: Staying on the subject of תורה learning, the גמרא brings a saying about reviewing what you learn. Learning without review is compared to planting without harvesting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A farmer who plants but never harvests did all the work and gets nothing from it. In the same way, learning without חזרה means the effort never turns into lasting knowledge.

keyTerms.meaning: Reviews it (חזרה, going over one's learning again)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
Anyone who learns Torah
and does not review it
is similar to a person
who plants and does not harvest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the פסוק to related teachings about תורה learning, connected to רבי נהוראי's point about learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה without reviewing it is like planting without harvesting.

steps.title: Forgetting one's learning is like burying a newborn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע compares someone who learns תורה and lets it be forgotten to a woman who gives birth and then buries her child.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: Anyone who learns Torah and lets himself forget it is like a woman who gives birth and then buries her child.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, sharper saying is added. Learning תורה and then forgetting it is compared to losing a newborn baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה's picture was a harvest that never came. רבי יהושע's picture is more painful: something real was produced and then lost. The word 'משכחה' suggests the person himself causes the forgetting through neglect.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
Anyone who learns Torah and causes it to be forgotten
phrases.notes: The wording means he lets himself forget it, for example by not reviewing.

phrases.english: is similar to a woman
who gives birth and buries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger comparison on the same theme of keeping one's learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה and letting it be forgotten is like giving birth and burying the child.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's teaching begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to quote רבי עקיבא. His actual words continue in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening of the next saying. The גמרא is introducing רבי עקיבא, and his words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is stated here yet. This line introduces the next teaching in the same series about תורה learning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Attribution line only; content continues in the following text
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the next saying in the series on תורה learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening attribution only; the statement itself follows.
